verdict.rationale: Sentry documents a first-party self-hosted distribution that lets you run all of Sentry on your own server, so you control where data lives. The API docs also reference organization region-specific domains, which implies regional hosting. However, no evidence shows that SaaS users can explicitly select a data-residency region, and the self-hosted setup is 'minimal' with no guarantees or dedicated support. Missing for 10: documented SaaS region/residency selection (e.g., US vs EU) at org creation, a list of available regions with residency guarantees, and independent corroboration of residency controls.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: How you can run all of Sentry on your own server, without paying anything.
Using your organization's region-specific domain will generally result in lower latency for most API calls.
This version comes with no guarantees or dedicated support.
